title: Sparrow brief: feedback graft and low-cost patches
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of small, high-frequency customer asks we can "graft" into the platform without a major product cycle. This doc is intentionally scrappy — prioritize clarity over polish.

Context: over the last 6 weeks CS has logged ~120 runtime-related tickets that are small individually but cluster around a handful of operational friction points (see sample quotes below). Customers are losing confidence in predictable behavior when they hit these edge cases; many can be addressed with documentation, runtime toggles, or tiny behavior changes.

Top themes (ranked by frequency & perceived impact):

- KV cache invalidation confusion: customers expect prefix-based cache hints to persist across model rollouts; when we switch model variants they lose previously cached prefixes and see latency spikes.
- Opaque fallbacks & tooling: users want clearer signals when fallbacks are used (which model, why, and whether tokens were truncated).
- Token accounting surprises at the SDK boundary: a few SDKs add invisible separators/metadata which inflates token counts for customers without clear billing ties.
- Short-sequence throughput regression: some customers with many short requests saw throughput drops after batching heuristics changed — wants per-route sampling and an opt-in conservative batching mode.

Representative customer snippets (anonymized):

- "We rolled a smaller LLM variant and overnight our prefix-based caching stopped working — billing stayed the same but latency doubled." — mid-market search product
- "Our audit logs show 'fallback to compatible-model' but no context; we had to escalate to CS to understand why two dangerous requests used the tiny model." — healthcare platform
- "Embedding costs spiked after SDK update. We suspect the client started adding \"\n\n\t\" separators somewhere upstream." — analytics company

Proposed low-cost patches (fast experiments, target 1–2 sprints each):

1) KV-cache migration hint: lightweight metadata header that signals compatibility of a cached prefix across model variants.
   - What: add header x-rw-cache-compat: <compat-id> produced during model pinning operations. On rollout, server attempts to map compat-id to new variant before invalidating cache.
   - Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Derek) + CS doc (Marisol)
   - Rough effort: 3 dev-days + 1 doc day
   - Success metric: reduce cache-miss-induced latency spikes on rollouts by 60% in pilot customers (sample of 6).
   - Risks: subtle correctness if model architecture differs significantly; we'll gate behind model-compat registry.
   - Linked artifact: JIRA-3421

2) Fallback transparency headers + console flag:
   - What: emit structured header and console event when automatic fallback triggers (fields: fallback-reason, from-model, to-model, truncated-tokens). Add a per-route flag in Console to enable verbose fallback traces for a tenant.
   - Owner: product-console + observability (Sofia)
   - Effort: 5 dev-days front/back + console UI spike
   - Success metric: CS time-to-first-meaningful-response down from median 8h to <1h for fallback cases in first 30 days

3) SDK token delta audit mode:
   - What: SDK hook that can be toggled to emit token-delta diffs for a sample of requests (client-side) so we can identify invisible separators or serialization artifacts.
   - Owner: developer-experience (Liam)
   - Effort: 2 dev-days + instrumentation rollout
   - Success metric: identify top 3 token-delta sources for several affected customers within 2 weeks.

4) Conservative-batching per-route opt-in:
   - What: add a route config flag `conservative_batching: true` that reduces wait windows and caps batch size for routes known to be latency-sensitive with short sequences.
   - Owner: serving-runtime + product-hosted-api
   - Effort: 4 dev-days + rollout notes
   - Success metric: throughput for short-seq routes returns to pre-regression baseline for pilot tenants.

Operational playbook (how CS will run pilots):

- Week 0: recruit 4–8 customers from field who flagged the problem (mix of enterprise + mid-market). Get explicit consent for telemetry during pilot.
- Week 1: apply patch behind feature flag for single-tenant rollout; monitor latency, token counts, and error rates.
- Week 2: iterate on instrumentation + docs, widen to 50% of pilot tenants.
- Week 3–4: measure outcomes, prepare concise one-pager for eng/product decision.

Cost/benefit rough math (example for KV header):

- If an affected customer has 2M requests/day and rollouts induce a 2x latency/cost bump on 1% of requests for 3 days -> saving from reduced cold misses can be ~ $X/day (placeholder). We'll compute with actual metrics when pilot users are onboarded.

Notes to self / unresolved: 

- Need a model-compatibility registry design doc (where will compatibility ids live? how to surface to oncall?)
- SDK telemetry needs a privacy review — ensure no PII in diffs. Loop in security.
- For fallbacks: decide whether console flag exposes raw token contents in traces (likely no) — consider redaction by default.

Slack / Jira pointers: 

- Filed tickets: JIRA-3421 (KV header prototype), JIRA-3499 (fallback telemetry), JIRA-3508 (SDK audit hook).
- Field threads: slack:#cs-field thread pinned under "sparrow-pilot-2027".

Immediate next steps (this week):

- [Marisol] Send targeted outreach to 6 customers asking for telemetry consent and short intake form.
- [Derek] Prototype server header mapping model-compat -> variant mapping. Quick spike branch.
- [Liam] Add token-delta toggle to SDK dev branch and ship sample build for two customers.
- [Sofia] Wire up console flag mockup and capture cost of exposing extra traces (observability quotas).

If we get traction: package as a Q2 quickpatch bundle (3–4 items) and present as an ops-plus-docs release targeting low-risk impact customers first.

Appendix: quick intake form (copy-paste)

- Short description of the problem you're seeing (paste logs if helpful)
- Which model(s) and routes are affected?
- Are you on Dedicated / Hosted / Private?
- Can we enable verbose telemetry for 2 weeks? (yes/no)
- Point of contact + timezone

End notes: keep this lightweight. The aim is to reduce operational pain for customers with small investments and clear rollback paths. This is intended to be a living scratchpad; move items that gain traction into proper RFCs and product tickets.
